newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Prods-Midco gasolines rally, Gulf eases.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Prods-Midco gasolines rally, Gulf eases.

text.p: Midcontinent differentials leapt higher again by late Friday as helped by the Explorer Pipeline's move to tighten rules for shipments from the Gulf for the remaining three cycles of May.
New York Harbor gasolines also firmed by late Friday, with prompt reformulated gasolines jumping sharply early in the day, according to traders, while US Gulf prices were steady to flat.
++ Gasoline differentials firmed one cent for the second day in a row as traders attempted to short cover after the Explorer's recent announcement of tightened rules for shipments from the Gulf.
Group Three conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 4.25 cents over the June print, while Chicago material saw offers widen to 2.75 cents over.

The Explorer, which ships from Texas as far north as Indiana, said Wednesday that transfer of line space between cycles will not be allowed for the remaining 13th, 14th and 15th ten-day cycles of May because the pipeline is running at capacity.

Traders said players with commitments to deliver barrels by early June are beginning to round up physical barrels early because the Explorer is five to 10 days behind schedule and is not expected to deliver 14th cycle barrels until after June 3.

++ Prompt low sulphur 74-grade diesel differentials stood at around 1.40 cents under June futures, after briefly moving up and getting done at levels as firm as 1.25 cents before again receding to 1.40 cents under. With action so light, diesel did not appear poised to weaken further.
"It's been very, very, very quiet today," said one trader.
Traders had some difficulty identifying the source of the diesel selling in Houston, but some said it could be a midcontinent refiner coming out of maintenance in Illinois.
Traders said "M1" regular unleaded gasoline weakened Friday, with prompt bids down to 3.70 cents under June NYMEX unleaded -- just a touch firmer than M1 differentials at the beginning of the week.
Looking ahead, some saw prices in Houston firming as the scramble for barrels first in the midcontinent then in New York begin heating up.
Prompt reformulated A2 conventional gasoline surged early in the day, with barrels changing hands at 1.90 cents over the June NYMEX price, traders said.
However, that strength was concentrated in the nearby material, with A2 for delivery early next week seen offered at 1.10 cents over the June NYMEX.
Regular M2 conventional gasoline trailed the gains in the reformulated material, with prompt barrels trading at 1.05 and 1.15 cents over the June NYMEX.
